tldr: Minari is an open-source Python library adhering to Gymnasium standards and integrating with HuggingFace Hub to enable offline RL dataset collection, sharing, and complete environment reproduction in a single line of code. It provides 338 high-quality datasets, including a full regeneration of deprecated D4RL, and natively interfaces with major RL training libraries.
overview:
Offline reinforcement learning—learning policies solely from previously collected interaction data—has attracted immense interest in domains where trial-and-error is costly, such as physical robotics. However, the research community has long struggled with a major issue: sharing and reproducing datasets is extraordinarily difficult. There has been no standard data format, and widely used benchmarks like D4RL remain tethered to outdated simulator environments, leaving them impossible to regenerate once environment code moves on.

To tackle this, a team at the Farama Foundation developed Minari, a new infrastructure designed around the familiar interface of Gymnasium, the de facto standard for RL environments. With Minari, recording a dataset simply requires wrapping an existing Gymnasium environment. Essential metadata—including random seeds, applied wrappers, and exact pip package requirements—is recorded alongside the trajectories. Furthermore, seamless integration with HuggingFace Hub allows users to publish and download datasets with a single command.

To validate its practical utility, the team regenerated all D4RL tasks using modern Gymnasium and MuJoCo, releasing a total of 338 reproducible datasets (55 million steps) spanning robotic manipulation, navigation, and beyond. They also benchmarked six offline RL algorithms on the regenerated data to confirm its reliability as an evaluation suite. Minari effectively introduces a common language for dataset sharing in reinforcement learning.
contributions: Formulated an environment-agnostic unified format and released an open-source Python library for dataset collection, processing, and HuggingFace Hub sharing with Gymnasium-style ergonomics.
Built an infrastructure that records environment specifications, random seeds, wrapper stacks, and pip requirements to ensure complete reproducibility and regeneration of data generation pipelines.
Provided 338 diverse, large-scale reproducible datasets (350K trajectories, 55M steps), including a full modern regeneration of D4RL which previously depended on deprecated MuJoCo setups.
Established native integrations with major RL training libraries like TorchRL, AgileRL, and d3rlpy, allowing users to load datasets and begin training with a single line of code.

sections.heading: Why Has Sharing Offline RL Data Been So Difficult?
sections.summary: Agent interaction data is immensely valuable, but the lack of a standardized format and reproducibility issues from simulator updates have severely hampered sharing. Minari resolves this by providing a Gymnasium-compliant API to create, share, and load datasets under a shared infrastructure.
sections.details:
Interaction data collected by robots through trial-and-error is extremely expensive to acquire. Ideally, such data should be shared across the community as a valuable asset for subsequent research. In practice, however, only a small fraction of datasets are shared in a format that other researchers can readily reuse.

Three major obstacles have created this bottleneck. First is the **lack of a shared format**. Different benchmarks structure observations, actions, and episode boundaries idiosyncratically, forcing researchers to write custom data loaders from scratch every time they evaluate a new dataset. Second is the **loss of reproducibility due to static snapshots**. Most published datasets are static dumps without recorded simulator versions, wrappers, or random seeds. When the underlying simulator updates, recreating identical evaluation setups or regenerating data becomes impossible. D4RL, the standard offline RL benchmark, is a prime example: it remains trapped on deprecated versions of Gym and MuJoCo. Third is the **friction of multi-source integration**. Combining data from different sources requires manual reconciliation of spaces and missing metadata.

Minari is an open-source library built specifically to resolve these issues. Its key design choice is following the Gymnasium conventions already familiar to RL researchers. Recording a dataset is as simple as wrapping an environment and stepping through it, and loading requires only one line of code. Just as Gymnasium established the standard interface for environments, Minari aims to become the standard interface for offline RL datasets.

sections.heading: How Minari Differs from Prior Benchmarks and Libraries
sections.summary: Prior efforts were either restricted to static dataset releases or tied to specific deep learning frameworks and robotics setups. Minari is framework-agnostic, empowers users to create and publish their own datasets, and ships with built-in, end-to-end environment recovery.
sections.details:
Existing tools in offline RL have largely fallen into two categories: fixed benchmark distributions and framework-specific tooling.

### RLDS
RLDS, developed by Google, provides an expressive schema for RL trajectories. However, because it is built on top of TensorFlow Datasets, using it in PyTorch or JAX codebases—the dominant frameworks in contemporary RL research—introduces an unwanted, heavyweight dependency on TensorFlow.

### D4RL and RL Unplugged
D4RL established offline RL as an active research field, but it relies on deprecated versions of `gym` and `mujoco-py` without publishing reproducible data generation setups. Consequently, maintaining or regenerating it has become unsustainable. Similarly, DeepMind's RL Unplugged is a collection of static datasets and lacks tooling for users to generate new, compatible datasets of their own.

### LeRobot and HuggingFace Hub
LeRobot provides models and datasets for real-world robotics on PyTorch and HuggingFace Hub, but its schema is specialized for multi-camera streams and robot joint states. Minari, by contrast, targets universal compatibility with any Gymnasium space (images, vectors, text, etc.), whether in simulation or on real hardware. In addition, because HuggingFace Hub itself does not interpret RL episodic structure, Minari acts as an orchestration layer managing episodes and spaces on top of it.

sections.heading: Ready to Train: Native Integrations with Major Libraries
sections.summary: Minari is integrated out of the box with leading offline RL libraries: TorchRL, AgileRL, and d3rlpy. Researchers can switch datasets in existing training scripts with a single line of code instead of writing custom loaders.
sections.details:
No matter how well-engineered a dataset format is, it will not gain traction unless popular training libraries support it natively. Crucially, Minari already integrates with three major offline RL libraries.

### TorchRL
In TorchRL, the official reinforcement learning library in the PyTorch ecosystem, Minari datasets can be loaded directly into replay buffers. They interface seamlessly with TorchRL's modular environments and agent architectures.

### AgileRL
AgileRL specializes in evolutionary hyperparameter optimization and population-based training, drastically reducing algorithm tuning overhead. It natively supports loading Minari datasets out of the box.

### d3rlpy
As one of the most widely used offline RL libraries implementing algorithms like CQL, BCQ, and TD3+BC, d3rlpy allows users to load Minari datasets directly using its scikit-learn-like API.

As a result, when exploring a newly published Minari dataset, researchers do not need to write conversion scripts; swapping a single dataset name parameter in their training code is all it takes to begin experimentation.

sections.heading: Gymnasium-Aligned Design and Built-In Reproducibility
sections.summary: Minari adopts Gymnasium naming conventions and nested space structures, supporting episode filtering, slicing, and HDF5/Arrow storage. By recording environment specs, seeds, wrappers, and pip requirements, it guarantees exact environment reconstruction and data regeneration.
sections.details:
### 4.1 Dataset Standards
Minari dataset IDs follow a hierarchical naming convention: `namespace/environment/dataset_name-v0`. Aligned with Gymnasium environment IDs, this gives users immediate insight into the originating environment, task variant, and version. Datasets are organized as sequences of episodes, supporting complex observation and action spaces including nested Dict, Tuple, and Text spaces. Notably, Minari explicitly differentiates between environment `truncations` (timeouts) and `terminations` (task completion). Conflating timeouts with terminal states introduces severe value estimation bias in offline RL, making this separation essential.

### 4.2 Software Package Features
Minari can be installed simply via `pip install minari` and handles four primary operations: creating, loading, manipulating, and sharing datasets. Applying the `DataCollector` wrapper to an environment automatically records all steps taken by an agent. Data collected outside Gymnasium, such as real-world robot logs, can also be converted through standard buffer APIs. A comprehensive CLI allows users to publish and retrieve datasets using `minari upload` and `minari download` via the HuggingFace Hub.

### 4.3 Ensuring Rock-Solid Reproducibility
A classic failure mode in offline RL occurs when the environment used during evaluation subtly diverges from the environment used to generate the dataset. Minor differences in time limits, missing observation wrappers, or small simulator updates alter physics behavior, rendering benchmark score comparisons invalid. Minari addresses this via three mechanisms:
- **Environment & Wrapper Recovery**: Calling `dataset.recover_environment()` reconstructs the identical Gymnasium environment alongside the exact wrapper stack used during data collection.
- **Seed Tracking**: The starting seed of every episode is recorded, enabling exact trajectory regeneration when paired with deterministic policies.
- **Pinned Software Requirements**: Pinned pip package requirements are stored in the dataset metadata, and Minari checks for version discrepancies when recovering environments.

sections.heading: 338 Ready-to-Use Datasets: From Regenerated D4RL to Web Navigation
sections.summary: The authors host 338 datasets comprising 350K trajectories, 55M steps, and 56GB of storage. This library spans a fully regenerated D4RL benchmark, modern MuJoCo environments, language-conditioned BabyAI, Atari, MetaWorld robotics, and web navigation logs.
sections.details:
Alongside the library release, 338 datasets totaling 55 million steps (approx. 56GB) were published to HuggingFace Hub. All dataset generation scripts are fully open-source, allowing anyone to regenerate or modify them.

### 5.1 D4RL Regeneration
The legacy D4RL benchmark has been fully regenerated using modern Gymnasium, Gymnasium-Robotics, and official MuJoCo Python bindings. While internal simulator updates mean trajectories are not bitwise identical to the originals, they provide clean, reproducible datasets generated through identical procedures. This includes Ant Maze, Point Maze, the 24-DoF Adroit hand tasks, Franka Kitchen, and MiniGrid navigation.

### 5.2 Modern MuJoCo Environments
Covering standard Gymnasium MuJoCo environments, data was collected using checkpoints trained via Stable Baselines3 (SAC and TQC). Because offline RL benchmarking requires diverse data quality, datasets are partitioned into skill tiers such as `expert`, `medium`, and `simple`.

### 5.3 BabyAI, Atari, MetaWorld, and WebAgents
Minari also includes diverse suites addressing varied AI and robotics research needs:
- **BabyAI**: 170 datasets featuring language-conditioned instruction following with Text observation spaces (e.g., "put the blue ball next to the red box").
- **Atari**: Covering 57 ALE games with raw RGB frames rather than preprocessed pixels, using JPEG compression to substantially reduce download footprints.
- **MetaWorld**: 50 robotic manipulation tasks performed with a simulated Sawyer arm, well-suited for multi-task and transfer learning research.
- **WebAgents**: A converted version of WebLINX text data for web browser navigation (~24K steps), demonstrating Minari's ability to support non-simulation sequential decision tasks.

sections.heading: Benchmarking with Six Offline RL Algorithms
sections.summary: Using CORL, the authors evaluated six offline RL algorithms—BC, BC-10%, TD3+BC, AWAC, CQL, and IQL—on the regenerated D4RL and MuJoCo datasets. The results confirm that the relative task difficulty hierarchy is preserved, establishing a reliable baseline for future research.
sections.details:
When a benchmark dataset is regenerated from scratch, researchers need to know whether standard algorithms can still learn effectively on it. To verify this, the authors benchmarked six offline RL algorithms (BC, BC-10%, TD3+BC, AWAC, CQL, and IQL) using CORL, a library of clean offline RL implementations.

### Insights from Benchmark Results
The experiments confirmed that the regenerated D4RL datasets faithfully retain the difficulty profile of the original benchmarks. For example, on the Adroit expert datasets, imitation-based methods (BC, AWAC, IQL) achieve scores above 100. Conversely, on complex tasks containing human demonstrations or cloned policies (`door`, `hammer`, `relocate`), all methods stay below 27.6, preserving their status as challenging open problems.

IQL proved exceptionally stable across the suite, matching previously reported CORL scores closely (e.g., 87.7 vs. 87.5 on `antmaze/umaze`, and 106.1 vs. 106.7 on `door/expert`).

### Nuances When Comparing to Historical Baselines
The authors also candidly noted discrepancies compared to older published results. First, BC and AWAC achieved higher scores on large Ant Maze tasks than previously reported, which is likely attributable to updated maze implementations and cleaner planner trajectories. Second, CQL struggled on Ant Maze and collapsed on `hammer` and `relocate`, while TD3+BC failed on `door` and `relocate`. This occurred because default CORL hyperparameters (such as state normalization toggles in CQL) were kept unchanged rather than overfitted to the new datasets. These scores provide a transparent baseline for reproducible future comparisons.

sections.heading: Long-Term Maintenance, Hosting, and Open Governance
sections.summary: Minari does not rely on transient grant funding; it is maintained by the non-profit Farama Foundation under an open-source MIT license. Datasets are permanently hosted on HuggingFace Hub, and all data generation scripts are publicly shared.
sections.details:
A recurring failure mode for academic software tools is project abandonment once original authors graduate or grant funding lapses, causing repositories to break within a few years.

Minari is structurally protected against this. It is maintained by the Farama Foundation, the non-profit consortium responsible for Gymnasium, PettingZoo, and other foundational RL libraries. This governance model ensures ongoing updates, maintenance, and community support beyond the lifecycle of individual research grants.

Minari is released under the permissive MIT license and developed openly on GitHub and PyPI. Datasets are hosted on HuggingFace Hub's free, permanent storage infrastructure, while generation scripts reside in a dedicated public repository. Third-party datasets like WebLINX clearly retain their original licensing and author attribution in metadata, establishing a transparent ecosystem where the community can confidently build and contribute.

sections.heading: The Gymnasium Moment for RL Datasets
sections.summary: Minari brings the standardization to offline RL datasets that Gymnasium brought to RL environments. Despite known limitations regarding lifelong tasks and non-deterministic physics, it provides a dependable, community-driven platform for dataset sharing and research.
sections.details:
Minari marks an inflection point where both dataset recording and training pipelines can rely on a shared standard. Data recorded today via a Gymnasium wrapper can be shared globally with a single CLI command, and years later, researchers can reconstruct the exact environment using preserved seeds and dependency metadata to evaluate new algorithms fairly.

At the same time, the authors outline clear limitations:
- **Episodic Boundary Dependency**: Because Minari structures and samples data by episode, it is less suited out of the box for lifelong learning or open-ended environments without clear episodic boundaries.
- **Storage Overhead**: Minari prioritizes generic format compatibility, meaning raw I/O throughput may lag behind bespoke, highly tuned custom loaders built for specialized large-scale distributed setups.
- **Simulator Non-determinism**: While Minari captures exact seeds and environment versions, it cannot guarantee bitwise identical trajectories if the underlying physics engine contains non-deterministic operations.

Even with these caveats, by delivering 338 reproducible datasets alongside a robust toolkit, Minari gives offline RL a shared foundation, allowing researchers to stop reinventing data loaders and focus on advancing algorithms.

sections.heading: Appendix: Metadata Specifications, Spaces, and Episode Formats
sections.summary: The appendix details the dataset and episode-level metadata schemas, support for all Gymnasium spaces including nested and Text spaces, and the programmatic structures used to access episode data in Python.
sections.details:
The paper's appendix specifies the internal architectural design of Minari datasets.

### Metadata Schema (Appendix A)
At the dataset level, Minari records the dataset ID, total episode and step counts, observation and action space definitions, links to generation code, author information, algorithm names used during data collection, and pinned pip requirements. At the episode level, summary statistics including minimum, maximum, mean, standard deviation, and sum of rewards (return) are precomputed. This enables rapid filtering—such as extracting the top 10% highest-return trajectories for filtered behavioral cloning (BC-10%)—without needing to load entire gigabyte-scale datasets into memory.

### Flexible Spaces and Episode Structures (Appendix B, C)
Minari fully supports standard Box and Discrete spaces, as well as MultiBinary, MultiDiscrete, Text spaces, and arbitrary nestings of Dict and Tuple spaces. In Python, loaded `MinariDataset` objects yield `EpisodeData` instances upon iteration or sampling. These instances provide structured access to `observations`, `actions`, `rewards`, `terminations`, and `truncations`. Regardless of observation complexity, the interaction API remains clean and uniform across all tasks.

takeaways: Researchers struggling with broken, unmaintained D4RL dependencies can switch to Minari's fully regenerated D4RL suite running on modern Gymnasium and MuJoCo.
Collecting offline RL datasets requires only wrapping a Gymnasium environment with `DataCollector`, which automatically logs seeds and environment requirements.
Users of TorchRL, d3rlpy, or AgileRL can immediately train on Minari's 338 datasets by changing just a single line in their existing data loading code.
limitations: Managing and sampling data at the episode level makes Minari less suited for open-ended or lifelong RL problems that lack distinct episode boundaries.
The standardized data representation introduces storage and serialization overhead that may be slower than bespoke data loaders tailored to specific distributed pipelines.
Environment recovery depends on deterministic simulator implementations; simulators with internal non-determinism cannot be perfectly reproduced from seeds alone.
